clue.text: Favourite in theatre company's return helping in the performance

indicators.note: the favourite sits inside the other two pieces joined together
a return goes back the way it came, so the theatre company is read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a repertory theatre company
a helping is a ration, a portion of food
a favourite is a pet

explanation.surface: A star player in a touring company helps out with the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns REP into PER; PET then goes in between PER and RATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Perpetration is the carrying out of a deed, usually a crime, so it is a kind of performance.

clue.text: Graphically describe river fish? About right

indicators.note: about means round, so the river and fish go round the right

parts.note: the Po is the river of northern Italy
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Asking how to draw a river fish, with a confirmation that is about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts RT inside PO and RAY together.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray is to depict vividly in words or pictures.

clue.text: Tease a young woman for being a dummy

parts.note: to rag is to tease
doll is old slang for an attractive young woman

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a girl for being foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag doll is a soft cloth figure, a stuffed dummy.

clue.text: Delighted when decent characters governed the centre

indicators.note: governed takes the centre of the shuffled letters
the characters of decent, its letters, are used in a new order

parts.note: ran means governed

explanation.surface: Joy when respectable people took control of the middle ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'characters' of decent are rearranged to ENTCED, and RAN goes into its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Entranced means enchanted, filled with wonder and delight.

clue.text: Miss Aylmer's emblem in the wars

definitions.meaning: Rose Aylmer is the subject of Landor's poem
the red and white flowers of Lancaster and York gave the Wars of the ... their name; the plural answer covers both badges

explanation.surface: A lady's badge was carried in the battles.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose is the forename in the possessive, and the flowers were the badges of the rival houses in England's 15th-century civil wars.

clue.text: They're noted for producing rolls in the kitchen

definitions.text: They're noted for producing rolls in the kitchen

parts.words: They're noted for producing rolls in the kitchen
parts.note: sounds like bakers making bread, but means drums written in musical notation that play drum rolls in an orchestra's kitchen, its percussion section

explanation.surface: Bakers famous for making bread rolls at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen is orchestral slang for the percussion section, and a roll is a rapid drumbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Kettledrums are notated in the score and played with rolls, sitting in the percussion section.

clue.text: Grain product from Malta — extremely obscure variety

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so the letters are rearranged
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An unusual cereal food imported from Malta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes O and E from obscure, which join MALTA to be shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal is ground oats, a cereal food.

clue.text: Horse making commotion endlessly upset people on strike

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word upside down, reading it backwards
the commotion loses its final letter

parts.note: a fuss is a commotion
folk are people
to punch is to strike

explanation.surface: A horse causing an endless fuss among workers on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts FUSS to FUS, and 'upset' turns that to SUF.
explanation.definitionFit: A Suffolk Punch is a heavy draught breed from the English county of Suffolk.

clue.text: Honest enough to get the post

definitions.meaning: a vertical post, as in goalposts or a door frame

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a person of integrity, and a vertical structural support.

clue.text: It indicates rejection of afterthought about this compiler's cat

indicators.note: rejecting something turns it back, so the afterthought is read backwards
the reversed afterthought goes round the compiler's word

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an afterthought at the end of a letter
the compiler speaking of themself says 'my'
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A setter's pet cat is having its afterthoughts rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts MY inside PS to give PMYS, and 'rejection of' turns the whole of that back to SYMP before TOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A symptom is a sign that points to an illness, something that indicates it.

clue.text: False declaration intended, it's said, to support gallery founder's daughter?

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the rest

parts.note: an unmarried daughter is Miss
Sir Henry Tate founded the Tate Gallery in London

indicators.note: it's said means the word for intended is heard, not spelt

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A lie meant to back up the claims of an art patron's daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate founder's daughter would be Miss Tate; MENT is said like MEANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A misstatement is an untrue or inaccurate assertion.

clue.text: Enormous in shape, a former Chinese island

indicators.note: the outsize letters sit inside the shape and the a

parts.note: form means shape
OS is the abbreviation for outsize, used on clothes labels

explanation.surface: A description of a huge old island off China.
explanation.definitionFit: Formosa is the old Portuguese-derived name for Taiwan, an island formerly ruled by China.

clue.text: Sort of ageless ability to keep 8 on board

indicators.note: to sort is to rearrange, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: An ageless knack for staying upright aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 refers to the answer to 8 Across, UPRIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Having one's sea legs means being able to walk steadily and stay upright on a rolling ship.

clue.text: Faithful ally in difficulties without cipher

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the shuffled ally goes round the cipher
a word in difficulties is in disarray, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: a cipher is a zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A faithful friend gets into trouble without a secret code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in difficulties' scrambles ALLY to LYAL, and 'without' means outside, so it goes round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyal and faithful are synonyms, both meaning steadfast in allegiance.

clue.text: Vehicle caught by sailor allowed.. outside port

indicators.note: the three pieces together go round the port

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
AB is an able seaman
let means allowed
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A sailor is let ashore at a port and catches a ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabriolet is a light horse-drawn carriage, and now a convertible car.

clue.text: One seeking advantage in simpler surroundings?

indicators.note: advantage is placed inside the plainer word

parts.note: simpler surroundings are barer ones, with less in them
a gain is an advantage

explanation.surface: Someone hoping to profit in a more basic setting.
explanation.walkthrough: GAIN goes inside BARER, after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A haggler at market is one seeking a better price, a good deal.

clue.text: Food for a salesman

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a vender, or vendor, is one who sells

explanation.surface: Something to eat, offered in favour of a travelling seller.
explanation.definitionFit: Provender is fodder or provisions, an old word for food.

clue.text: Doubter disposed to be too much in evidence

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so the letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: A sceptic inclined to make himself too conspicuous.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtrude is to thrust oneself forward and become unduly noticeable.

clue.text: Great circle, as seen cutting into eastern peak

indicators.note: the word for as cuts into the east and peak pieces

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or peak
qua is Latin for as, in the capacity of

explanation.surface: A big round shape seen slicing into a mountain to the east.
explanation.walkthrough: QUA means 'as' (from Latin); a TOR is a rocky hill in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A great circle is any circle on a sphere centred at its middle, the line round Earth's middle being one.

clue.text: Power of fighter to knock one' out

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter plane

indicators.note: out signals that the letter for one is dropped from the knock

parts.note: to hit is to knock
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A boxer's strength lies in knocking an opponent out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes I from HIT, leaving HT.
explanation.definitionFit: Might is strength or power.

clue.text: Sounds like a French nobleman's tent

indicators.note: the noble's title is heard rather than read

parts.note: a marquis is a French nobleman, said 'mar-kee'

explanation.surface: A French aristocrat's canvas shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquee is a large tent used for parties and shows.

clue.text: Common girl receiving rising Frenchman

indicators.note: the girl takes in the turned Frenchman

parts.note: gal is a girl

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: René is a French man's name

explanation.surface: An ordinary girl welcomes an up-and-coming man from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns RENE into ENER, which 'receiving' puts inside GAL.
explanation.definitionFit: General means common to many, widespread.

clue.text: Carved peg or tee sunk in hazard

indicators.note: a golf hazard such as a bunker puts things in disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A golfer's peg or tee has been lost in a bunker.
explanation.walkthrough: A hazard in golf is a bunker or water obstacle, which suits the tee.
explanation.definitionFit: A netsuke is a small carved Japanese toggle, used as a peg to hang things from a sash.

clue.text: Put up with losing king's supply

indicators.note: the word for put up with loses the king's letter

parts.note: to endure is to put up with
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: Tolerating the loss of a monarch's provisions.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is to endow or furnish someone with a quality.

clue.text: Bill the backward private a corporal in NATO, for example!

annotationWithheld.clue: Bill the backward private a corporal in NATO, for example!

clue.text: Obsessed, he had a relative smothered

indicators.note: the relative is wrapped inside the words for he had

parts.note: he had shortens to he'd
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: A man so obsessed that he smothered his aunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smothered' puts AUNT inside HED (he'd, short for he had).
explanation.definitionFit: To be haunted by something is to be gripped by it, preoccupied and obsessed.

clue.text: What's the matter? It's free of charge

definitions.text: What's the matter? It's free of charge

parts.words: What's the matter? It's free of charge
parts.note: reads as a question about a problem and a promise of no cost, but means a particle of matter with no electric charge

explanation.surface: A worried question answered with the reassurance that it costs nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: This subatomic particle in an atom's nucleus has no electrical charge, hence its name.

clue.text: Geo Rex, twice the source for a novelist

indicators.note: twice means the shortened Geo plus R is written two times

parts.note: Geo is the old abbreviation of George
R stands for Rex, king, as in GR on a pillar box
a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: King George is named twice as the inspiration for an author.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell was the pen name of the English writer of Animal Farm and Nineteen Eighty-Four.
